newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish PZU insurer 1996 audited loss PLN 170 mln.
newsitem.headline: Polish PZU insurer 1996 audited loss PLN 170 mln.

text.p: Poland's largest insurance firm, Powszechny Zaklad Ubezpieczen SA (PZU), showed a 170 million zloty loss in 1996 after audit, the company's president said on Thursday.
Jan Monkiewicz told a news conference that PZU's loss was mainly a result of fast growth in the number and average value of damages, which led to a high techical loss.
"The technical loss amounted to 345 million zlotys and this led to a 170-million net loss," he said.
"The reasons for the loss are fast growth in the number of damages which grew by 30 percent to 1.3 million, and in their average value which grew 32 percent to 1,700 zlotys," he added.

In its preliminary figures PZU had reported a 1996 loss of 92 million zlotys but company officials later said this had to be adjusted after the audit to accommodate technical reserves higher than originally planned.

Monkiewicz said PZU made a net profit of 204.9 million zlotys in the first quarter of this year and while the strong first quarter result was largely a seasonal phenomenon the company expected to return to profit for the whole of 1997.
